To set up ERPNext, first, follow the installation steps to start the server with `bench start`. Then, create a new site using `bench new-site erpnext.localhost`. To install the ERPNext app, use `bench get-app` followed by `bench --site erpnext.localhost install-app erpnext`. For a manual install on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, use `sudo python3 install.py --production --user Your_USERNAME --mariadb-version 10.5 --verbose`. Ensure to create a user with sudo rights and modify the install.py script if necessary. For Docker-based setups, refer to the Frappe Docker documentation for ARM-based setups.
To install ERPNext, follow the steps outlined in the README.md file on the GitHub repository. First, set up bench by following the installation steps and start the server with "bench start". Then, create a new site using "bench new-site erpnext.localhost". Next, get the ERPNext app with "bench get-app" and install it with "bench --site erpnext.localhost install-app erpnext". Finally, open the URL in your browser to see the app running. For more details, refer to the official documentation and Frappe School.
To install ERPNext, you can use the `frappe-bench` package from PyPI with `pip install frappe-bench`. This package is a command-line utility for installing, updating, and managing multiple sites for Frappe applications. It also fetches the required containers and sets up a default ERPNext instance. Alternatively, you can use `ws-frappe-cli` which is a command-line tool for setting up, configuring, and managing Frappe/ERPNext development environments. It provides an intuitive interface for common development tasks such as creating a new Frappe development environment, site creation, and app management. To install it, use `pip install ws-frappe-cli`.
1. Setup bench by following the Installation Steps and start the server

